# roughly

Hand-drawn marks are the loudest thing on a page. Used well, one mark tells the reader what to take away.
Used on everything, they are noise and the page looks like homework. Your job is mostly **editorial**:
choose the few things worth marking, then draw each one with the right tool, at the right size, in the
right place, and prove it on a screenshot.

`<skill>` below means this skill's directory.

## Files

| File | Read it when |
|---|---|
| `references/choosing.md` | **Always.** Which mark for which intent, and what each mark must never be used for. |
| `references/sizing.md` | **Always.** Stroke, padding, arrow size, label size and the clearance each mark needs, keyed to font size. |
| `references/color.md` | **Always.** One ink per page, dark vs light surfaces, highlighter pairs, semantic red/green. |
| `references/arrows.md` | **Any arrow.** Placement, the bend that lands the head on the target, size, label, failure → fix. |
| `references/composition.md` | More than one mark on a page, any arrow or sticky, or mobile layouts. |
| `references/recipes.md` | Before writing code: copy the closest recipe instead of improvising. |
| `references/setup.md` | Roughly isn't installed yet, or fonts / Tailwind are missing. |
| `references/pitfalls.md` | Something looks wrong on the screenshot, or you're annotating inside tables, cards, scroll areas, MDX. |
| `references/props.md` | Exact props of each component. Generated from the source; trust it over memory. |
| `scripts/check.mjs` | Lints annotation usage. `node <skill>/scripts/check.mjs <src dirs>`; `--setup` checks install + fonts. |
| `scripts/screenshot.mjs` | Real 1440px and 390px full-page screenshots with marks fully drawn. `node <skill>/scripts/screenshot.mjs <url>` |
| `assets/qa-gallery.tsx` | A page with every recipe on dark and light. Mount it to sanity-check an install. |

## Workflow

Copy this checklist into your reply and tick it off:

```
Annotation progress:
- [ ] 1. Setup: Roughly installed, fonts loaded (check.mjs --setup)
- [ ] 2. Editorial pass: candidates → keep ≤ budget, with a reason each
- [ ] 3. Pick the mark for each (choosing.md)
- [ ] 4. Size + clearance for each (sizing.md)
- [ ] 5. Colour (color.md) and order/timing (composition.md)
- [ ] 6. Write the code from recipes.md; semantic HTML underneath
- [ ] 7. check.mjs clean
- [ ] 8. Screenshots at 1440 and 390 read; collisions, clipping, overflow fixed
- [ ] 9. Report
```

### 1. Setup
Run `node <skill>/scripts/check.mjs --setup .` from the project root. Fix what it reports with
`references/setup.md` (install, fonts, Tailwind, `"use client"`). Don't start annotating until it passes:
missing fonts make arrow labels and sticky notes render in the body font, which looks broken.

### 2. Editorial pass — before any code
Read the page's copy. List every candidate as `text → why a reader must notice it`. Then cut:

- **Budget:** 1 mark per section/viewport. **At most 3 marks above the fold**, at most ~1 per 400 words of
  prose. A checklist (check marks on every row) or a price change (strike + circle) counts as one mark.
- Keep a candidate only if removing the mark would change what a skimming reader takes away.
- Never mark two things in the same sentence. Never mark the thing that is already the biggest/boldest
  element on screen unless the mark adds meaning (e.g. the price changed).
- If the user named exactly what to mark, mark that — but still apply the rest of this skill to *how*.

Show the user the kept list (and what you cut) when you're annotating a whole page.

### 3–5. Choose, size, colour
Use the three references. They're short tables; follow them rather than taste. The common mistakes they
prevent: circling a whole sentence, highlighting a paragraph, a 2px line under 72px type, a rainbow of
colours, red used for emphasis, arrows without a label, marks that run into the next word.

**Arrows get their own pass** (`references/arrows.md`): pick the empty side for `placement`, then **leave
`bend` unset**. The component picks the bend whose sign lands the head *into* the target; a hand-set bend
with the wrong sign makes the head skim along the target's edge (the most common broken-looking arrow).

### 6. Write it
Start from the closest recipe in `references/recipes.md`. Rules that always apply:

- **Next.js App Router: `"use client";` at the top of every file that uses `Roughly.*`.** In a Server
  Component the dot-components are `undefined` and the page crashes. If the page must stay a Server
  Component, move the annotated section into its own client component.
- **Meaning lives in the HTML, not the drawing.** The SVG is `aria-hidden`. Strike-through → wrap in
  `<del>` (and the new value in `<ins>`); highlight → `<mark>`; a cross mark → add `sr-only` text
  ("not included"). Screen readers and copy-paste must read correctly with the marks gone.
- **Reserve space.** Circles, boxes, arrows and sticky notes draw *outside* their element and take no
  layout space. Give every one the margin/padding from `sizing.md` or it will sit on top of neighbours.
- **Wrap only the words.** `<Roughly.Underline>` goes around the 1–4 key words, not the whole `<h1>`.
- Use the namespaced components (`Roughly.Circle`, `Roughly.Arrow`, …) — they take every prop.
  `<Roughly type="…">` exposes fewer props.
- Never put a rough mark on text that is still changing (typewriter effects, live counters) — it draws to
  the first size it measures.

### 7. Lint
`node <skill>/scripts/check.mjs <the files you touched>` → 0 errors. Every warning is fixed or you can say
why it's intentional.

### 8. Verify on screenshots — required
With the dev server running:
```bash
node <skill>/scripts/screenshot.mjs http://localhost:3000/ --name annotated
node <skill>/scripts/screenshot.mjs http://localhost:3000/pricing --selector "#plans" --name plans
```
It renders with reduced motion so marks are fully drawn, scrolls the page so scroll-triggered marks fire,
uses true 390px mobile emulation, and prints `✖` if the page is an error screen and `⚠` with the
offending elements if anything overflows horizontally. Fix those first. `--selector "#id"` crops to one
section (with room around it for arrows/stickies). **Read every image.** For each mark check:

- It sits where intended: underline under the words, circle centred, arrow tip 6–12px from the target
  and the **arrowhead pointing into it** (not lying along its edge; arrows.md › Checklist).
- Nothing overlaps: no mark crosses neighbouring text, another mark, a button edge, or gets clipped by a
  card (`overflow:hidden`).
- At 390px: arrows and stickies still fit, nothing causes horizontal scroll, multi-line wraps still look
  intentional. If not, use the mobile rules in `composition.md` (move, shrink or drop the mark).
- The page still reads as one hand: same ink, similar weights, nothing louder than the headline.

Fix, re-shoot, re-read. Never report done from code alone. If a mark is missing in a shot: re-run with
`--wait 5000`, then try `--segments` (one shot per screen; some pages relayout during full-page capture
and drop marks there) or `--selector` on that section, before assuming a bug.

### 9. Report
List each mark: the text, the mark, why. Say what you cut. Give the screenshot paths. Mention anything you
couldn't verify (no dev server, auth wall).

## Hard rules (the short version)

1. Fewer marks. 1 per section, ≤ 3 above the fold.
2. Mark type follows intent (`choosing.md`), never decoration.
3. Stroke scales with the text (`sizing.md`): ≈ font-size ÷ 14, between 1.5 and 4.
4. One ink colour per page; red only for removal/negative, green only for done/positive.
5. Every overlay mark gets reserved space; nothing touches neighbouring text.
6. Arrows always carry a short label (≤ 4 words) unless pointing at something self-explanatory. Don't set
   `bend` unless you keep its auto sign; the head must point into the target.
7. Semantic HTML under every mark; reduced motion is handled by the components — don't fight it.
8. Screenshots at 1440 and 390, read, before you say done.

# Arrows An arrow is the only mark that *moves the eye*, so it is the one most often drawn wrong: the head skims along the button instead of pointing into it, the arc is a loop, the tail sits on top of a headline, the label is in the body font. Work through the four decisions below in order and check each one on the screenshot. ## What you can set | Decision | Props | Default | Rule of thumb | |---|---|---|---| | **Where the tail comes from** | `placement` | `top-right` | The side of the target that is genuinely empty | | **How long / how close** | `size` (or exact `distance`, `offset`) | 1 → 65px long, 8px gap | Scale with the target (sizing.md › Arrow geometry) | | **How it curves** | `bend`, `variant` | auto, `curved` | **Leave `bend` unset**; it is chosen per placement | | **The head** | `arrowhead` | `open` | `filled` for small arrows (`size < 0.8`) or thin ink | | **The pen** | `strokeWidth`, `iterations`, `roughness`, `seed` | 2, 1, 1, auto | 1 pass; different `seed` per arrow on a page | | **The label** | `label`, `labelFont`, `labelFontSize`, `labelFontWeight` | –, `caveat`, per font, 400 | 1–4 words, 18–34px | | **Where the label sits** | `labelPlacement`, `labelDistance`, `labelRotate`, `labelOffsetX/Y`, `labelColor` | `auto`, 8, 0, 0, ink | Beyond the tail, in empty space; rotate ±2–5° at most | | **When** | `animationDelay`, `animationDuration` | 0, 800 | Last mark in the section (composition.md) | Where the tip lands: corner placements aim at 85% (`*-right`) or 15% (`*-left`) of the target's width, `top`/`bottom` at the centre, `left`/`right` at mid-height. The tail is `D = 65 × size` px away from the tip. ## 1. Placement: where is the empty space? `placement` names where the **tail** sits relative to the target. Look at the screenshot and pick the side with the most empty room (no text, no other mark, not the viewport edge): ``` top-left top top-right ↘ ↓ ↙ left → [ target ] ← right ↗ ↑ ↖ bottom-left bottom bottom-right ``` - Corners (`top-right`, `bottom-right`, …) are the default choice: diagonal arrows read as hand-drawn and leave the label beside the target, not on top of it. - `left` / `right` for inputs and inline words with a margin beside them. - `top` / `bottom` for nav items, tabs, or centred targets with room above/below. - Never let the tail or label start on top of text. If no side is empty, reserve space (sizing.md) or drop the arrow. ## 2. Bend: leave it unset The arc's bend decides **where the head points**. The curve leaves the tail and arrives at the tip rotated `atan(3 × bend)` away from the straight tail→tip line. Turned one way, the head points *into* the target's edge; turned the other way, it lies flat along the edge or points away from it, which looks broken even though the tip is in the right place. When `bend` is omitted, the component picks the sign and depth that land the head **head-on (within ~15°)** for that placement: | `placement` | auto `bend` | Head arrives | Arc bows | |---|---|---|---| | `top-right` | **+0.32** | straight down into the top edge | up and over, like a hump | | `top-left` | **−0.32** | straight down into the top edge | up and over (mirror) | | `bottom-right` | **−0.32** | straight up into the bottom edge | down and under | | `bottom-left` | **+0.32** | straight up into the bottom edge | down and under (mirror) | | `top` | +0.2 | down | gentle | | `bottom` | −0.2 | up | gentle | | `left` | +0.2 | rightward into the left edge | gentle, rising | | `right` | −0.2 | leftward into the right edge | gentle, rising | On very wide targets (> 400px: a hero heading, a full-width screenshot) the corner tail sits far from the tip and the auto bend lands 15–25° off. Deepen it to ±0.4 (same sign), or use `size` 1.4+. `variant="s-curve"` arrives on the other side of its chord, so its auto sign is flipped; it is handled for you. `variant="straight"` ignores `bend`. **If you need a different depth**, keep the auto sign and change only the size: | Look | Corner placements | Side placements | Arc depth (sagitta ≈ 0.75 × bend × length) | |---|---|---|---| | Subtle, almost straight | ±0.2 | ±0.1 | ~15% / ~8% of the length | | **Natural hand-drawn (auto)** | **±0.32** | **±0.2** | **~24% / ~15%** | | Expressive swoop | ±0.4–0.5 | ±0.3 | ~30–38% | | Too much: a loop, head overshoots | > ±0.5 | > ±0.35 | — | What the wrong sign does (target 120px wide, `size={1}`), measured as how far the head is off "pointing straight in": | `placement` | Right sign (auto) | Wrong sign, same depth | |---|---|---| | corner, e.g. `bottom-right` | −0.32 → **~2°** | +0.32 → **~90°** (lies along the bottom edge) | | side, e.g. `right` | −0.2 → **~14°** | +0.2 → **~48°** (head points down, past the target) | So never flip `bend` to move an arc away from text. **Move the arrow instead** (another placement, or more reserved space). `check.mjs` reports a wrong sign as `arrow/bend-sign`. ## 3. Size and gap | Target | `size` | `strokeWidth` | `labelFontSize` | Head | |---|---|---|---|---| | Inline word, icon, dot | 0.6–0.8 | 1.5 | 18–20 | `filled` reads better this small | | Button, input, badge, card | 0.9–1.2 | 2–2.5 | 20–24 | `open` | | Hero heading, screenshot region | 1.4–1.8 | 2.5–3 | 26–34 | `open` | - The head length is ~16% of the arrow's length (7–24px) and never less than 3.5 × `strokeWidth`. A short, thick arrow gets a big head; if it looks clumsy, lower `strokeWidth` rather than `size`. - The tip stops `8 × size` px from the target. Keep it 6–12px: closer looks like it's stabbing the target, further looks like it's pointing at the gap. Use `offset` for exact pixels on very small or very large targets. - Use `distance` (exact length in px) only when the empty space is a fixed size, e.g. a 90px gutter. ## 4. Label - 1–4 words, lowercase, taken from the page ("free, no card" only if the page says so). See choosing.md. - `labelPlacement="auto"` puts it beyond the tail on the side the arrow comes from. Override it only when that side is crowded: `left`/`right` for a corner arrow near a column edge, `top`/`bottom` for side arrows. - `labelDistance` 6–12. Below 4 the label touches the tail; above 16 it stops reading as the arrow's label. - `labelRotate` −5…5 adds a hand-written tilt. Leave it 0 when there are two arrows; mixed tilts look messy. - The label is in Caveat/Kalam/Reenie Beanie. If it renders in the body font, the fonts aren't loaded (setup.md › Fonts). - `labelOffsetX/Y` are for a final nudge of a few px after reading the screenshot, not for layout. ## Pointing at a spot, not an element To point at part of an image or screenshot, wrap a zero-size element positioned on that spot: ```tsx
{/* the spot: 72% across, 30% down */}
``` With a near-zero target the corner tip offsets (85% / 15% of the width) vanish, and the arrow lands on the spot itself. ## Several arrows on one page - At most 2 per page and never 2 in one viewport (composition.md). - Same `size`, `strokeWidth` and ink, so they read as one hand; different `seed` so they don't look stamped. - Never cross each other or another mark's drawn area; never two arrows at the same target. - Mirror placements across a layout (left column `bottom-left`, right column `bottom-right`) rather than pointing both the same way. ## Checklist on the screenshot For every arrow: 1. **The head points into the target**, roughly perpendicular to the edge it lands on. If it skims along the edge, the bend sign is wrong: remove `bend`. 2. The tip is 6–12px from the target, not touching it, not floating far off. 3. The arc bows into empty space and doesn't cross text, the target, or another mark. 4. The label is in the handwriting font, fully visible, and ≥ 8px from any other text. 5. Nothing clipped by an `overflow:hidden` ancestor; at 390px, nothing past the viewport edge (switch to a `bottom-*` placement or drop it on mobile: composition.md › Mobile). ## Failure → fix | On the screenshot | Cause | Fix | |---|---|---| | Head lies along the target's edge / points past it | `bend` sign wrong for the placement | Delete `bend` (auto), or keep the auto sign | | Arc is a loop or half-circle | `|bend|` > 0.5 | Corners 0.2–0.4, sides 0.1–0.3 | | Arrow looks ruler-straight and mechanical | `variant="straight"` or `bend` ≈ 0 | Remove both (auto) | | Huge head on a small arrow | thick `strokeWidth` on `size < 0.8` | `strokeWidth` 1.5, or `arrowhead="filled"` | | Tip touches / overlaps the button | `offset` too small or negative | Remove `offset` (8 × size) or 8–10 | | Tail or label sits on a headline | Wrong placement, or no reserved space | Pick the empty side; reserve space (sizing.md) | | Label far from the tail | `labelDistance` large, or offsets used for layout | `labelDistance` 6–12, offsets 0 | | Two arrows look identical | Same placement and no `seed` | Different `seed`, or mirrored placements |

# Choosing the mark

Pick by **what you want the reader to do**, not by what looks fun. Each mark has a meaning readers already
know from paper: an underline says "this matters", a circle says "look at this one thing", a strike says
"this is gone". Using a mark against its meaning confuses people even if they can't say why.

## Decision table

| The reader should… | Mark | Component | Target |
|---|---|---|---|
| Take away the key claim of a headline | **Underline** (single) | `Roughly.Underline` | 1–4 words, the payload of the sentence ("this weekend", not "Ship your") |
| Spot one number, price, or word among similar ones | **Circle** | `Roughly.Circle` | 1–3 short words or a number, **one line only** |
| Actually read one sentence in a block of prose | **Highlight** | `Roughly.Highlight` | One sentence or clause (≤ ~15 words). Never a paragraph |
| See a UI element / badge / button / value as an object | **Box** | `Roughly.Box` | An element with edges, or a short code/value. Not running prose |
| Treat several lines/items as one group | **Bracket** | `Roughly.Bracket` | ≥ 2 lines. Curly `{` = "these belong together"; square `[` = quoted/excerpted block |
| Know a value was replaced | **Strike-through** + the new value | `Roughly.Strike` | The old value, with the new one right after it. Never a strike on its own |
| Know an option was rejected/ruled out | **Cross-off** | `Roughly.Cross` | Short item (a word, a plan name, a card). Pair with the winner being marked |
| See yes/no per row of a list | **Check / cross mark** in the margin | `Roughly.Check` | Every row of the list gets a mark, or none does |
| Look at something they'd otherwise miss, with a reason | **Arrow + label** | `Roughly.Arrow` | A button, an input, a screenshot detail. Label ≤ 4 words |
| Get an aside / tip about an element | **Sticky note** | `Roughly.Sticky` | ≤ 12 words. Max 1 per page |
| Feel a personal touch (signature, sign-off word) | **Handwriting** | `Roughly.Handwriting` | ≤ 6 words, ≤ 50 chars (hard cap). Decorative only |

## Per-mark rules

### Underline
- Variants: `single` (default — use this), `double` (strong, ≤ 1 per page, for "this is the one"), `wavy`
  (playful/informal tone only; also implies "questionable" in editing — avoid in serious contexts).
- **Keep the target on one line**: add `className="whitespace-nowrap"` to the underline. A key phrase split across two lines reads as two separate marks, and when the line break shifts after the mark is measured (font swap, responsive type) the underline lands on the wrong line. If the phrase is too long to stay on one line on mobile, it is too long to underline.
- Never underline links or text that looks like a link (readers will click it). If the target *is* a link,
  use a highlight or circle instead.
- Never underline a whole multi-line headline. Pick the words.

### Circle
- For a single item that must pop out of a row of peers: the price among plans, the number among stats,
  the one word in a sentence.
- **One line only.** If the target can wrap at 390px, add `whitespace-nowrap` or choose another mark.
- Don't circle buttons (use a box or an arrow) or whole cards (use a box or a sticky).

### Highlight
- The marker sits *behind* the text. Text contrast against the highlighter colour must stay ≥ 4.5:1 — see
  `color.md` for safe pairs. This is the one mark that changes legibility.
- Wrap the text in `<mark>` (reset its default background) so the meaning survives without the drawing.
- Highlights are calm; they suit testimonials, docs, articles. In a hero, prefer an underline.

### Box
- Use for things that already are objects: a badge ("Most popular"), an input, a toggle, a key/value, a code
  token. It reads as "this thing here".
- `variant="single"` for small targets (< 24px tall), `double` (default) for headings or big targets.
- Not for paragraphs (multi-line boxes look like errors) — use a bracket.

### Bracket
- For 2+ lines that share one point: a group of warnings, a set of steps, a quote. Side `left` is the
  default reading position; `right` works when the left edge is aligned to a grid you don't want to break.
- `bracketStyle="curly"` (group) or `"square"` (excerpt/quote). `side="both"` only for a pulled quote.
- It renders as a `div` and pads the content itself — don't wrap inline text with it.

### Strike-through
- Always followed by the replacement (`$29 → $9`, `useFetcher() → useQuery()`), and wrapped in `<del>`, with
  the new value in `<ins>`. A strike with no replacement just looks like a mistake left on the page.
- `single` for prices and code; `double`/`triple` only for a deliberate, playful "NO".
- Red ink (it means removal).

### Cross-off
- For rejected options in a comparison: the competitor's feature, the old way, the plan you don't
  recommend. Pair it with a positive mark on the alternative (check, circle) so it's a contrast, not a
  random X.
- Keep targets short — a big X over a paragraph is unreadable. Pass `padding` so the X clears the text.

### Check (margin marks)
- `mark="check"` or `mark="cross"`, in the left margin (`side="left"`, default). Use `as="li"` inside `<ul>`.
- Consistency: every item in the list gets a mark. Crosses only for features truly not included, with
  `sr-only` text ("not included").
- `checked` can be toggled for an interactive checklist; it draws/erases.
- Stagger rows by 120–180ms so the list "ticks down".

### Arrow + label
- Points *from* empty space *to* the target. `placement` names where the arrow comes from (`top-right` =
  the tail sits above-right of the target).
- Label: 1–4 words, lowercase, conversational ("free, no card", "start here", "new"). Never a sentence.
- **Never invent a claim for a label.** Take it from the page ("14-day trial" only if the page says so). If
  the page offers nothing beyond the button text, use a neutral direction ("start here") or drop the arrow.
- No label only when the target is self-explanatory and the arrow is pure direction ("look here" is not a
  label — drop it).
- Max 1–2 arrows per page; never two arrows pointing at the same thing; never arrows crossing.
- `variant="curved"` (default) and **no `bend` prop**: the auto bend lands the head on the target for each
  placement. `straight` looks mechanical; `s-curve` only for long hops (≥ 120px) across whitespace.
  Everything else about arrows (size, gap, label, failures): `arrows.md`.

### Sticky note
- A paper note with tape or pin. It's an aside: tips, "drag to reorder", "we're hiring". Max 1 per page.
- `pin="tape"` (default) for a casual tip, `pin="pin"` for "notice board" style, `none` for minimal.
- Keep the default yellow paper unless the page's palette fights it; never more than one paper colour.

### Handwriting
- Draws real glyph outlines from a handwriting font (`caveat`, `kalam`, `reenie-beanie`). Use for a
  signature or one emotional word. Max 6 words / 50 chars.
- It's an SVG drawing, so also keep the text in the DOM for screen readers and search (the recipe shows how).

## Combinations that work

- **Price change**: strike old + circle new = one idea, one mark budget.
- **Comparison**: cross-off on the rejected column + check marks on the chosen column.
- **Hero**: underline the key words + one arrow with label at the primary CTA, drawn in that order.
- **Docs**: bracket a group of steps + a highlight on the one line people get wrong (two separate sections).

## Combinations that don't

- Two marks on the same words (circle + underline, highlight + box).
- Circle + arrow pointing at the same circle (the circle already points).
- Highlight in a hero headline and an underline in the subtitle (competing emphasis).
- Sticky + arrow + circle in the same viewport — pick one.

# Colour

## The rules

1. **Always pass `color`.** Each Roughly type has a different default (indigo underline, pink circle,
   emerald box, amber arrow, red strike…). Leaving defaults on gives you a rainbow.
2. **One ink per page.** Every non-semantic mark (underline, circle, box, bracket, arrow + label,
   handwriting) uses the same ink, like one pen. Define it once: `const INK = "#FCD34D";`
3. **Semantic colours only for semantic marks.** Red = removed / wrong / not included (strike, cross-off,
   cross mark). Green = done / included (check mark). Never use red for emphasis or green for decoration.
4. **At most 2 emphasis hues on screen**: the ink + the highlighter (or the ink + one semantic colour).
   A checklist's green checks and red crosses are one semantic pair and don't break this rule.
5. **Contrast.** Strokes need ≥ 3:1 against the background (WCAG non-text). Highlighted text needs ≥ 4.5:1
   against the highlighter colour (as blended over the page).

## Picking the ink

Use the site's accent colour if it passes 3:1 against the background; otherwise shift it lighter (on dark)
or darker (on light) until it does. If the site is monochrome/neutral, use a pencil ink (below) or
amber — a warm hand-drawn colour reads as "a person wrote this" against a cold UI.

### Dark surfaces (background lightness < ~25%)

| Ink | Hex | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Amber (default pick) | `#FCD34D` | Most pages. Warm, legible, reads as a marker |
| Sky | `#7DD3FC` | Cool/technical brands |
| Rose | `#FDA4AF` | Playful brands (not near red semantic marks) |
| Lime | `#BEF264` | Energetic; avoid next to green check marks |
| Chalk / pencil | `#E7E5E4` | Monochrome design systems; subtle, editorial |

Avoid mid-tone saturated colours (`#6366F1`, `#EC4899`, `#10B981`) as stroke ink on near-black: they sit
around 3–4.5:1 and thin strokes look muddy.

| Highlighter on dark | Hex | `opacity` | Text colour |
|---|---|---|---|
| Indigo (default) | `#4338CA` | 0.85 | white / neutral-100 |
| Plum | `#6D28D9` | 0.8 | white |
| Deep teal | `#0F766E` | 0.85 | white |
| Amber-brown | `#92400E` | 0.85 | white |

Never a light highlighter (yellow-200) under white text on a dark page — the text vanishes.

### Light surfaces

| Ink | Hex | Use |
|---|---|---|

### Sticky notes

Paper `#FDE68A` (default yellow) with ink `#3B2A14` works on both dark and light pages. Alternatives:
`#FBCFE8` pink, `#BAE6FD` blue, `#D9F99D` green — one paper colour per page. The label ink stays dark
brown/graphite regardless of the page ink: it's written on paper, not on the page.

## Pages with both themes

If the site switches light/dark, the ink must switch too. Read the theme the same way the site does
(e.g. `useTheme()` from next-themes, a `dark` class on `<html>`, or a CSS variable) and pick from the tables:

```tsx
const { resolvedTheme } = useTheme();
const INK = resolvedTheme === "dark" ? "#FCD34D" : "#2563EB";
```

Pass a real colour value (hex/rgb). Don't pass `var(--…)`: several marks write the colour into SVG
`stroke`/`fill` attributes, where CSS variables aren't reliable.

## Images and colourful backgrounds

On photos, gradients or brand-coloured sections, test the ink on the screenshot. If any part of the stroke
drops below 3:1 against what's behind it, switch to white (dark/busy image) or graphite (light image), and
consider a slightly heavier stroke (+0.5).

# Composition: several marks, timing, layout, mobile

## Budget

| Area | Max marks |
|---|---|
| Above the fold / hero | 3 (typically: 1 underline + 1 arrow, or 1 circle) |
| Any other section | 1 (a checklist or a price change counts as one) |
| Long-form article | ~1 per 400 words, never 2 in a paragraph |
| Sticky notes | 1 per page |
| Arrows | 2 per page, never 2 in one viewport |

If everything is marked, nothing is. When in doubt, cut the weaker mark.

What counts as **one** mark:
- A price change (strike + circle on the same price).
- A list with a check/cross on every row (one idea: "here's what you get").
- A cross-off column plus the check column it's compared with.

What **doesn't count**: a sign-off signature (decorative, at the end of the page).

Pricing pages: per-plan feature checklists are a normal pattern and count as the cards section's one mark —
then don't add another mark inside the cards (circle the price *or* check the features, not both). In
prose, ~330 words allows 1 mark; ~800 allows 2.

## Hierarchy

The mark should be *one step louder* than the text it marks, not the loudest thing on the page.
- The headline mark gets the heaviest stroke on the page; marks lower down are lighter (sizing.md).
- Don't put a heavier mark in a sub-section than in the hero.
- Never mark the primary CTA with a circle or box (it already has a button shape); point at it with an arrow
  + label, or leave it.

## Order and timing (when animated)

Marks draw when they scroll into view. Within one viewport, choreograph them in **reading order**:

1. The page/section settles first: first mark at `animationDelay` 300–500ms (lets entry animations and
   fonts finish, and the reader land).
2. Then each following mark +250–400ms after the previous one *starts* (they overlap slightly, like a hand
   moving on).
3. Arrows last: they point at something the reader already saw.
4. List check marks: +120–180ms per row.

Total sequence in one viewport ≤ ~2s. Separate sections need no coordination: each fires on scroll.

```tsx
<Roughly.Underline animationDelay={400}>…</Roughly.Underline>      {/* 1. claim */}
<Roughly.Circle animationDelay={750}>…</Roughly.Circle>            {/* 2. number */}
<Roughly.Arrow animationDelay={1100} label="start here">…</Roughly.Arrow> {/* 3. CTA */}
```

`animate={false}` draws instantly — right for marks inside content that re-renders a lot (tables, editors),
print styles, screenshots/OG images. Reduced motion is handled automatically: when the visitor asks for it,
every mark renders fully drawn with no animation. Don't add your own `prefers-reduced-motion` logic.

## Placement and spacing

- **Arrows point inward**: tail in empty space (margin, gutter, whitespace beside a button), tip at the
  target. Pick the `placement` whose side of the target is empty. Never route an arrow across text.
- **Labels must not touch other text.** Check the label's box against headlines/buttons on the screenshot.
- **Two marks need ≥ 24px between their drawn edges** (including circle/box padding and arrow tails).
  Exception: the two halves of one idea (strike on the old price + circle on the new) may sit 8–16px apart —
  they're read together.
- Overlay marks may extend into the page gutter (a circle on the first item of a left-aligned row pokes out
  past the column edge); that's fine as long as it stays inside the viewport and isn't clipped.
- Marks inside cards: make sure the card doesn't clip (`overflow:hidden`, `overflow-x-auto`, `rounded` +
  `overflow-hidden` images). Either give the mark room inside the padding or move the mark outside the
  clipped element. See pitfalls.md.
- **Sticky notes** overlap the target's corner (`offset` negative) or sit in clear whitespace beside it —
  never covering content the reader needs.

## Mobile (390px)

Overlay marks don't move out of the way on narrow screens; check every one on the 390px shot.

| Problem at 390px | Fix |
|---|---|
| Arrow/sticky on the `right`/`left` runs off-screen or causes horizontal scroll | Switch to a `bottom-*` / `top-*` placement on mobile (hook below), or hide it below `sm` |
| Circle target wraps onto two lines | `whitespace-nowrap` on the target, or underline instead |
| Reserved side padding (`pr-[170px]`) squeezes content | Make it responsive: `pb-[120px] sm:pb-0 sm:pr-[170px]` together with the placement switch |
| Too many marks in one small screen | Drop the lowest-value one on mobile: render that text without its mark when `useIsNarrow()` is true |
| Underline target wraps onto two lines | Reads as two marks and can mis-draw after layout shifts. `whitespace-nowrap` on the underline; if that overflows at 390px, underline fewer words |

A tiny hook for responsive placement (no dependency):

```tsx
"use client";
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";

export function useIsNarrow(query = "(max-width: 639px)") {
  const [narrow, setNarrow] = useState(false);
  useEffect(() => {
    const mq = window.matchMedia(query);
    const update = () => setNarrow(mq.matches);
    update();
    mq.addEventListener("change", update);
    return () => mq.removeEventListener("change", update);
  }, [query]);
  return narrow;
}

// usage
const narrow = useIsNarrow();
<Roughly.Sticky placement={narrow ? "bottom-right" : "right"} … />
```

(`useIsNarrow` reads the media query after mount, so it's hydration-safe.)

## Static images / decks / print

For OG images, screenshots, PDFs or slides captured from the page: `animate={false}` on every mark, and
capture after `document.fonts.ready`.

# Pitfalls: symptom → cause → fix

## On the screenshot

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Circle/box loop runs over the neighbouring word | Overlay marks take no layout space | Margin = padding + stroke on that side (sizing.md › Clearance) |
| Circle cuts through the caption/line below | The ellipse wraps the font's content box (~1.2em), taller than a tight line box | `margin-bottom ≥ paddingY + 0.2em + stroke` |
| Underline drawn on the wrong line / only part of it | Target wrapped, and the layout shifted after it was measured (font swap, responsive type) | `className="whitespace-nowrap"` on the underline, or fewer words |
| A highlighted/struck phrase jumps onto its own line and the paragraph reflows | Older Roughly version wrapped multiline marks in `inline-block` | Re-install (`npx shadcn@latest add https://www.voidui.in/r/roughly.json --overwrite`), or pass `className="!inline"` |
| Error page: "Element type is invalid… got: undefined" | `Roughly.X` used in a Server Component | `"use client"` at the top of the file (Structure › Server Components) |
| Arrow or sticky cut off at an edge | An ancestor has `overflow:hidden` / `overflow-x-auto` / `overflow-clip`, or the viewport edge | Reserve space inside the clipping box, move the mark out of it, or change `placement` |
| Horizontal scrollbar at 390px (screenshot.mjs warns) | Reserved side space or a side placement doesn't fit | Responsive placement (`useIsNarrow`) and responsive padding; see composition.md › Mobile |
| Highlight invisible | Marker drawn at z-index −1 slipped behind an opaque parent background | `isolate` (isolation: isolate) on the nearest block parent |
| Highlighted text hard to read | Light marker under light text or dark marker under dark text | Use the pairs in color.md |
| Arrowhead lies along the target's edge or points past it | `bend` set with the wrong sign for the placement (e.g. `bottom-right` with a positive bend) | Remove `bend`; the auto bend lands the head head-on (arrows.md › Bend) |
| Arrow is a loop / half-circle | `bend` beyond ±0.5 | Remove it, or ±0.2–0.4 with the auto sign |
| Arrowhead looks oversized | Thick stroke on a short arrow (head ≥ 3.5 × stroke) | `strokeWidth` 1.5 for `size < 0.8`, or `arrowhead="filled"` |
| Arrow label in the page font, not handwriting | Caveat/Kalam/Reenie Beanie not loaded | setup.md › Fonts |
| Handwriting doesn't render | Font file 404 and the CDN fallback is blocked (CSP/offline) | Put the TTFs in `public/fonts/` |
| Mark offset from its text after load | Web font swapped in after measuring and something stopped the remeasure (fixed widths, `transform: scale` ancestors) | Marks re-measure on resize and `document.fonts.ready`; avoid animating `scale` on an annotated ancestor; or set `animate={false}` and render after fonts load |
| Mark drawn at the wrong place inside an animated/scaled container | rough-notation measures with `getBoundingClientRect`; transforms during entry animations distort it | Delay the mark (`animationDelay` > the container's animation) or annotate outside the transformed element |
| Marks missing in a screenshot | Captured before they drew | Re-run `screenshot.mjs` with `--wait 5000` (it already forces reduced motion so marks render finished) |
| Two marks fighting | Too many marks in one viewport | Cut one (composition.md › Budget) |
| Colours look random | `color` not passed; each type has a different default | Pass the one ink everywhere |

## Structure

- **Tables**: never annotate a `<td>`/`<tr>` directly (rough-notation inserts an SVG sibling, which breaks
  table layout). Wrap the cell content in a `<span>` and annotate that.
- **Lists**: use `Roughly.Check as="li"` directly inside `<ul>`; other marks go *inside* the `<li>`.
- **Links and buttons**: put the mark inside the `<a>`/`<button>` around the text, or around the whole
  element for a box/arrow. Don't underline links (they look like links already — use highlight or circle).
- **Flex/grid children**: overlay marks are `inline-block`; in a flex row they become flex items, so the
  row's `gap` doesn't include the drawing. Add margin as in sizing.md.
- **MDX / markdown**: import Roughly in the MDX file (or provide it via `components`) and wrap the words:
  `Ship it <Roughly.Underline color="#FCD34D" className="whitespace-nowrap">today</Roughly.Underline>.` Keep
  marks out of headings that generate anchor IDs if the slug would pick up odd text.
- **Server Components (Next.js App Router)**: `Roughly.Underline` and the other dot-components are
  **undefined inside a Server Component** ("Element type is invalid… got: undefined"): a client module
  imported into a server file is a reference proxy that doesn't carry static members. Either put
  `"use client";` at the top of the file that uses them (simplest for a page/section), or move the
  annotated section into a small client component and render that from the server page. `check.mjs` flags
  files under `app/` that use `Roughly.*` without `"use client"`.
- **Changing text**: the marks re-measure when `children` change, but don't annotate text that animates its
  width (typewriters, counters). Mark the stable word next to it.

## Accessibility

- The drawings are `aria-hidden`. Meaning must be in the markup:
  - strike → `<del>` (old) + `<ins>` (new)
  - highlight → `<mark>` (reset its background: `bg-transparent text-inherit`)
  - cross mark in a list → `sr-only` "(not included)"
  - handwriting → the real text in an `sr-only` span, the drawing `aria-hidden`
  - arrow label / sticky note → plain text in the DOM, readable as is; keep it meaningful out of context
- Reduced motion: handled by the components (they render fully drawn). Don't add your own handling.
- Colour isn't the only signal: cross vs check differ in shape, strike vs underline in position.

# Setup

Run `node <skill>/scripts/check.mjs --setup .` from the project root first; it tells you which of these

## Requirements

- React 18+ (Next.js, Vite, Remix, Astro islands… anything that renders React on the client).
- Tailwind CSS v3.4+ or v4 (the components use Tailwind classes, including arbitrary values).
- Node 22+ only for this skill's scripts.

## 1. Install the components

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add https://www.voidui.in/r/roughly.json
```

This writes the files under your `components/ui` alias (typically `components/ui/roughly/Roughly.tsx` and
`components/ui/roughly/roughly/*.tsx`) and installs `framer-motion`, `rough-notation`, `roughjs` and
`opentype.js`. Find where they landed:

```bash
# from the project root
ls components/ui/roughly 2>/dev/null || ls src/components/ui/roughly
```

Import:

```tsx
import { Roughly } from "@/components/ui/roughly/Roughly";
```

No shadcn setup (`components.json`)? Run `npx shadcn@latest init` first, or fetch
`https://www.voidui.in/r/roughly.json` and write each `files[].content` to its `path` yourself, then
`npm i framer-motion rough-notation roughjs opentype.js`.

If the project uses a different alias or folder, adjust the import paths in the recipes — never copy a
second set of the components.

## 2. Fonts

Arrow labels and sticky notes use **Caveat** (default), **Kalam** or **Reenie Beanie** by font-family name.
If the font isn't loaded the label silently renders in the page font, which looks wrong. Load the ones you use.

### Any framework (simplest)

In the document `<head>` (Next.js App Router: in `app/layout.tsx` inside `<head>`; Vite: `index.html`):

```html
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com" />
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin />
<link
  rel="stylesheet"
  href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Caveat:wght@400..700&family=Kalam:wght@300;400;700&family=Reenie+Beanie&display=swap"
/>
```

Or the CSS `@import` in `assets/fonts.css` at the top of your global stylesheet.

### Next.js with next/font (Caveat only)

`next/font` renames font families, so it only works for Caveat, through the `--font-caveat` variable the
components read. See `assets/fonts-next.tsx`:

```tsx
import { Caveat } from "next/font/google";
const caveat = Caveat({ subsets: ["latin"], variable: "--font-caveat" });
// <html className={caveat.variable}>
```

Kalam / Reenie Beanie still need the `<link>` above if you use them.

### Handwriting component (`Roughly.Handwriting`)

It parses the actual font file to draw glyph outlines. It first tries `/fonts/Caveat-Regular.ttf`,
`/fonts/Kalam-Regular.ttf`, `/fonts/ReenieBeanie-Regular.ttf` from your public folder, then falls back to
GitHub's raw Google Fonts files. For production, put the files in `public/fonts/` (and if you have a CSP,
the fallback host won't be allowed anyway):

```bash
mkdir -p public/fonts
curl -L -o public/fonts/Caveat-Regular.ttf "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/fonts/main/ofl/caveat/Caveat%5Bwght%5D.ttf"
curl -L -o public/fonts/Kalam-Regular.ttf "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/fonts/main/ofl/kalam/Kalam-Regular.ttf"
curl -L -o public/fonts/ReenieBeanie-Regular.ttf "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/fonts/main/ofl/reeniebeanie/ReenieBeanie.ttf"
```

Only download the ones you use. Or pass `fontUrl="/path/to/font.ttf"` for any TTF.

# Sizing and clearance

Everything scales with the **computed font size of the annotated text** (`fs`, in px). Find it from the
Tailwind class (`text-base` = 16, `text-lg` = 18, `text-xl` = 20, `text-2xl` = 24, `text-3xl` = 30,
`text-4xl` = 36, `text-5xl` = 48, `text-6xl` = 60, `text-7xl` = 72) or the CSS. For responsive type
(`text-4xl sm:text-6xl`) compute the stroke for both sizes; if they differ by more than 1, use the
**midpoint** (36px → 2.5 and 60px → 4 gives 3) and check both shots. Don't swap `strokeWidth` with a
media-query hook: one value that reads well at both sizes is more robust. Padding and clearance follow the
larger size (more room is harmless; too little overlaps).

These values were tuned on screenshots at 16, 32, 48 and 64px on dark and light pages.

## Stroke width

`strokeWidth ≈ fs / 14`, rounded to 0.5, clamped to **1.5 … 4**.

| Text | fs | Underline / circle / box / cross | Strike | Bracket | Arrow |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Small / UI | 12–14 | 1.5 | 1.5 | 1.5 | 1.5 |
| Body | 16–18 | 1.5–2 | 1.5 | 2 | 2 |
| Lead / H4 | 20–24 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| H3 / H2 | 28–36 | 2.5 | 2 | 2.5 | 2.5 |
| H1 | 40–48 | 3 | 2.5 | 3 | 2.5 |
| Hero | 56–80+ | 3.5–4 | 3 | 3 | 3 |

- Strikes are half a step lighter than other marks: the text must stay readable through them.
- Never below 1.5 (it disappears on low-DPI screens) or above 4 (it looks like a marker accident).
- `Check` marks size themselves from the line height; leave `size` and `strokeWidth` at defaults unless
  the list text is ≥ 24px (then `strokeWidth={3}`).
- Highlights don't take `strokeWidth` normally — the marker height follows the text. Leave it unset.

## Padding (how far the mark sits from the text)

| Mark | Prop | Formula | 16px | 32px | 48px | 64px |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Circle | `paddingX`, `paddingY` | 0.35em, 0.15em | 6, 3 | 11, 5 | 17, 7 | 22, 10 |
| Box | `padding={[y, x]}` | 0.2em, 0.4em (min 4, 8) | [4, 8] | [6, 13] | [10, 19] | [13, 26] |
| Highlight | `padding={[y, x]}` | 0.1em, 0.25em (min 2, 4) | [2, 4] | [3, 8] | [5, 12] | [6, 16] |
| Cross-off | `padding` | 0.3em (min 4) | 5 | 10 | 14 | 19 |
| Bracket | `bracketPadding` | 10–16 | 10 | 12 | 14 | 16 |
| Underline | — | fixed (sits ~4px under the baseline) | | | | |

The circle's defaults (`paddingX 22, paddingY 10`) are for display type; **always pass them for body
text**, or the loop swallows neighbouring words.

## Clearance (reserve space so marks don't sit on neighbours)

Circle, box, highlight, cross, arrow and sticky are drawn **outside** their element and take **no layout
space**. You must reserve it:

| Mark | Reserve |
|---|---|
| Circle | `margin-inline ≥ paddingX + strokeWidth`; `margin-block ≥ paddingY + 0.2em + strokeWidth` whenever there is text above/below (the ellipse is drawn around the font's content box, which is ~1.2em tall — taller than a tight line box) |
| Box | `margin ≥ padding + strokeWidth` on every side that has a neighbour |
| Highlight (inline) | none horizontally (it's a marker); keep `leading-normal` or more so lines don't overlap |
| Cross-off | same as its `padding` |
| Underline | ~6px below the line: keep `leading-snug` or more on the next line (headlines with `leading-none` collide). Always `whitespace-nowrap` on the target |
| Arrow | see below |
| Sticky | `width + offset + 12` on its side (the tilt adds ~12px) |

### Arrow geometry

`size` scales the whole arrow. Length `D = 65 × size` px, gap to the target `8 × size` px. The label sits
`labelDistance` (default 8) beyond the tail. Bend, head and label rules: `arrows.md`.

| Target | `size` | `strokeWidth` | `labelFontSize` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Inline word in body text | 0.7–0.8 | 1.5–2 | 18–20 |
| Button / input / card | 1–1.2 | 2–2.5 | 20–24 |
| Hero heading / big screenshot | 1.4–1.8 | 2.5–3 | 26–34 |

Label font size ≈ 1.2–1.5× the surrounding body text; Caveat (default) at < 18px is hard to read.

Space the arrow needs **beyond the target's edge**:

| `placement` | Block space (above/below) | Inline space (side) |
|---|---|---|
| `top-right` / `top-left` | above: `73·size + 8 + 1.2·labelFontSize` | right/left: `49·size + labelWidth/2` |
| `bottom-right` / `bottom-left` | below: same as above | right/left: same |
| `top` / `bottom` | that side: same | ~`23·size + labelWidth/2` to the right |
| `left` / `right` | none | that side: `73·size + 8 + labelWidth` |

`labelWidth` ≈ characters × 0.45 × `labelFontSize` for Caveat. Example: a `size={1.2}` arrow at
`bottom-right` of a button with "free, no card" at 24px needs ~120px below and ~140px to the right
(`pb-[120px] pr-[140px]` on the wrapper, or make sure that space is genuinely empty).

## Sticky note

| Prop | Value |
|---|---|
| `width` | 140–180 (150 default). Wider than 200 stops looking like a sticky |
| `fontSize` | 18–22 (Caveat) |
| text | ≤ 12 words → 2–3 lines |
| `rotate` | leave default (±4°); never more than ±8° |
| `offset` | 6 default; negative (-12…-24) to overlap the target's corner like it's stuck on |

## Handwriting

`fontSize` 36–56 for a signature, `strokeWidth` 1–1.5. Keep ≤ 6 words. It renders the glyph outlines; the
bigger it is the longer the draw (default duration 1200ms is right for 1–2 words; +300ms per extra word).

## Animation timing

| Mark | `animationDuration` | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Underline, strike | 500–700 (default 650) | short marks should be quick |
| Circle, box, highlight | 700–900 (default 800) | |
| Bracket | 600–800 | |
| Arrow | 700–900 (default 800) | head and label follow the shaft automatically |
| Check | 400–500 per row | stagger rows 120–180ms |
| Sticky | 450–600 | |

Total choreography of a section: ≤ 2s from first to last mark. See `composition.md` for ordering.
